content: Southampton Hospital, located in Southampton, New York, is a 168-bed medical facility and the only hospital serving the Hamptons region. It is part of the NewYork-Presbyterian Healthcare System. The hospital handles over 6,000 patient admissions annually and approximately 26,000 emergency room visits, with half of these occurring during the summer months. Notably, Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis, the former First Lady of the United States, and her sister Lee Radziwill were born at this hospital. The hospital's origins date back to 1908 when Dr. Wheelwright and Dr. Schenck performed an emergency surgery by kerosene light in the attic of a Southampton house because there was no time to transfer the patient to the nearest hospital. Following this event, they rented two rooms in a house on Hampton Road to establish a makeshift hospital. As demand for medical services grew, additional rooms were rented, and cots were placed in hallways to accommodate patients. In 1909, the Southampton Hospital Association purchased the Hervey J. Topping house at the corner of Lewis Street and Meeting House Lane, with plans to construct a hospital on an adjacent lot. In 1911, Samuel Parrish donated 2.5 acres of land on Old Town Road, extending from Meeting House Lane to Herrick Road. The current hospital was built on this site and opened in 1913. Since then, the hospital has undergone significant expansions. Southampton Hospital benefits from funds raised at the Hampton Classic Horse Show, a prominent social event during the summer season. However, in 2004, the hospital faced public backlash over a fundraising initiative called Southampton Plus. This program offered VIP hospital rooms and exclusive medical services, including 24/7 on-call medical advice, same-day doctor appointments, home visits, and access to VIP rooms, for fees of $3,800 for individuals and $6,000 for families. The plan was ultimately abandoned due to widespread criticism. The hospital is affiliated with several specialized centers and facilities, including: Westhampton Primary Care Center Centers for Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation in East Hampton and Westhampton Beach David E. Rogers, M.D. Center for HIV/AIDS Care Shinnecock Indian Health Clinic Southampton Care Center, a skilled nursing facility Southampton Hospital Regional Dialysis Center Center for Prenatal Care in Greenport Diagnostic centers in East Hampton and Hampton Bays In 2006, the Berger Commission, tasked with optimizing healthcare costs in New York State, recommended that Southampton Hospital reduce its capacity to 125 beds and merge with Eastern Long Island Hospital in Greenport and Peconic Medical Center in Riverhead. The proposal also strongly suggested that Brookhaven Memorial Medical Center in Brookhaven join the merged entity. The plan allowed the hospitals to continue operating independently but required formal affiliation with Stony Brook University Hospital. In 2007, Southampton Hospital announced plans to potentially sell its 12-acre property, located in a residential area, and construct a new hospital closer to a major highway. Although no specific location was disclosed, reports indicated that 400 of the hospital's 600 employees reside west of the Shinnecock Canal, which may influence the decision on the new site.
